newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.S. fights to stave off U.N. criticism of Israel.
newsitem.headline: U.S. fights to stave off U.N. criticism of Israel.

text.p: The United States urged an emergency session of the General Assembly on Friday to vote against a resolution demanding an immediate halt to Israel's construction of a new settlement in East Jerusalem.

Repeating U.S. criticism of Israel's decision to build 6,500 homes for Jews at a site called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic, U.S. Ambassador Bill Richardson said: "We regret that it was taken."
But he said U.N. bodies should "not insert themselves into issues" that Israel and the Palestinians had decided to address in their talks on "final status" matters.

"Today ... the United States urges members of this assembly to vote against the resolution before us, which we believe will actually make harder the difficult task before us: rebuilding confidence between the parties and reactivating a productive negotiation process," he said.

Richardson, whose government is the main sponsor of Middle East peace talks, followed a long list of speakers strongly criticial of Israel's action and supportive of the resolution, expected to be adopted by a large majority.

The United States last month vetoed two Security Council resolutions calling on Israel to abandon its building plan and voted against a similar resolution in the General Assembly, where it does not have veto power.

Calls by some speakers in the current assembly debate for collective action against Israel were "inconsistent with the responsibilities of this assembly and dangerous for the credibility of the United Nations," Richardson said.

He said the resolution "clearly infringes on the authority of the Security Council," alluding to a paragraph calling for "the cessation of all forms of assistance and support for illegal Israeli activities" in the occupied territories.

"By moving in the direction of endorsement of collective action directed against one of its member states, it sets a dangerous precedent, which could in the future be turned against any member state," he said.
Only the Security Council can impose mandatory sanctions. Resolutions of the assembly are not binding.

The 10th emergency assembly -- the first since 1982 -- was convened on Thursday at the request of Arab states under a 1950 procedure allowing for an issue considered a threat to peace to be transferred to the 185-member assembly if a veto prevents the 15-nation Security Council from taking action.

The United States used its council veto on March 7 and again on March 21 to block resolutions calling on Israel to abandon the Har Homa project. The United States and Israel cast the only negative votes when a non-emergency session of the General Assembly adopted a similar resolution on March 13 by a vote of 130 to two, with two abstentions.
